content.text:
## Root cause

`cmd /c start` was handing the OAuth URL to **cmd.exe, which treats an unquoted `&` as a command separator**. The URL was truncated at the first `&`.

`cmd/entire/cli/login.go:536` (as shipped in v0.10.0 — I confirmed via `git show v0.10.0`):

```go
case "windows":
    command = "cmd"
    args = []string{"/c", "start", "", browserURL}
```

Go's escaping doesn't save you here: `syscall.EscapeArg` only quotes an argument containing a space, tab, quote, or backslash. A URL has none of those, so it reaches cmd.exe bare.

The authorize URL is built with `url.Values.Encode()`, which sorts keys — so `client_id` comes first and `redirect_uri` sits behind three `&`s:

```
…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli&code_challenge=…&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=…
                                ^ cmd.exe cuts here
```

Leaving exactly `https://us.auth.entire.io/authorize?client_id=entire-cli` — byte-for-byte what your user reported, hence "missing redirect uri". Only the default browser flow is affected; `--device` isn't (see below).

It's macOS/Linux-only-tested code that's been broken since Mar 2026 (`5c44ffb87`), and only became user-visible when the browser redirect became the default login.

## Immediate workaround for the user

```
entire login --device
```

I verified against the live endpoint that its URL is `https://us.auth.entire.io/cli/auth?user_code=XXXX-XXXX` — a single query param, no `&`, so it survives cmd.exe intact. The device flow also prints the URL unconditionally, so copy-paste always works.

## Fix

Split the launcher per platform and, on Windows, call the Win32 `ShellExecute` API directly — no command line, so nothing to parse or escape. This is what `github.com/pkg/browser` switched to, and `golang.org/x/sys` was already a direct dependency.

- `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_windows.go` (new) — `ShellExecute` via a `shellExecute` seam for testing
- `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_other.go` (new) — `open`/`xdg-open`, unchanged behavior
- `cmd/entire/cli/login.go` — `openBrowser` keeps URL validation and the under-test guard, then delegates

Quoting alone wouldn't have been enough: the percent-encoded `redirect_uri` also exposes the URL to cmd's `%VAR%` expansion.

Tests: `browser_open_windows_test.go` asserts the whole URL reaches the shell association, plus a second test that executes `cmd /c echo <url>` to pin the truncation as the root cause so nobody reintroduces the shell. Both have `Windows` in the name, so the existing `test-windows` CI job (`-run '(Windows|MSYS)'`) picks them up. `browser_open_test.go` covers scheme validation cross-platform.

Verified: builds for darwin/windows/linux, `golangci-lint` clean on both darwin and `GOOS=windows` (the default run skips `_windows.go` files), and `mise run test:ci` passed. The Windows tests compile for windows/amd64 but I couldn't execute them here — they'll run on the CI Windows job.

## One thing worth deciding separately

`runBrowserLogin` (`login.go:289`) only prints the full URL when `openURL` returns an error. The truncated launch *succeeded* from our side, so the user got no copy-paste fallback — dead end. A successful browser spawn isn't proof the browser got a usable URL. I left that as-is since it's outside this bug, but printing the URL unconditionally (as the device flow does) would have made this self-service.

+package cli

+import (

+	"golang.org/x/sys/windows"
+)
+
+// shellExecute is the Win32 entry point openBrowserPlatform launches through.
+// It is a variable so the Windows test can capture the exact string handed to
+// the shell association without launching a real browser.
+var shellExecute = windows.ShellExecute
+
+// openBrowserPlatform hands browserURL to the Windows shell association for
+// its scheme, which is the user's default browser.
+//
+// This calls ShellExecute rather than spawning `cmd /c start` on purpose. An
+// OAuth authorization URL carries `&` between query parameters and `%XX`
+// inside the percent-encoded redirect_uri, and both are cmd.exe
+// metacharacters: `&` ends the command, `%VAR%` expands. Go's argv escaping
+// does not help, because syscall.EscapeArg only quotes arguments containing a
+// space, tab, quote, or backslash — a URL has none of those, so it reached
+// cmd.exe bare and the browser only ever saw the text before the first `&`.
+// ShellExecute takes the URL as a single wide string, so there is no command
+// line to parse and no escaping to get wrong.
+//
+// hwnd is 0 (no owner window — this is a console app) and the verb is nil so
+// the association's default verb ("open") applies. ShellExecute returns once
+// the browser has been asked to open the URL; there is no child process for us
+// to wait on or release.
+func openBrowserPlatform(_ context.Context, browserURL string) error {
+	if err := shellExecute(0, nil, windows.StringToUTF16Ptr(browserURL), nil, nil, windows.SW_SHOWNORMAL); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("open browser via ShellExecute: %w", err)
+	}
+	return nil
+}

#### Invoking Commands on Windows - Never Put a Dynamic Value on a cmd.exe Line

**When Entire performs the exec itself, do not go through `cmd.exe`.** Pass the
program and its arguments as separate argv elements (`exec.Command(prog, arg)`),
or call the Win32 API directly.

cmd.exe treats `&`, `|`, `<`, `>` as command separators/redirections and expands
`%VAR%`, and **Go's argv escaping will not protect you**: `syscall.EscapeArg`
only quotes an argument containing a space, tab, quote, or backslash. A URL,
a percent-encoded path, or any `&`-bearing string therefore reaches cmd.exe bare
and is silently cut at the first metacharacter. That is exactly how
`entire login` shipped a Windows build that opened
`…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli` and got rejected for a missing
`redirect_uri` — the `cmd /c start "" <url>` launcher lost everything from the
first `&` on, and because the truncation happened inside the released child, the
CLI saw a successful launch and printed no fallback URL.

Escaping is the right tool in exactly one situation: **a third party owns the
exec.** When Entire writes a command into an agent's config file (Cursor/Codex
`hooks.json`) and that agent runs it through cmd.exe, there is no shell to
avoid — use `agent.escapeWindowsCMD`. Reviewers should flag any new
`exec.Command("cmd", …)` / `"cmd.exe"` call site that interpolates a
non-constant value.

Key files: `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_windows.go` (ShellExecute, the
avoid-the-shell side) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_command.go`
(`escapeWindowsCMD`, the third-party-exec side). Each doc comment points at the
other.
